name: Augusta
title: Augusta Tanker Gauging | UTM at the Industrial Harbour
description: Ultrasonic thickness gauging at Augusta for crude and product tankers, chemical carriers and gas ships: cargo and ballast tank, deck and piping measurement.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement at the Port of Augusta, Sicily
intro: Augusta is a deep natural harbour on Sicily's east coast, serving the refineries and chemical plants of the Priolo and Melilli industrial area. Crude carriers, product tankers, chemical ships and gas carriers queue at its roadstead and berths. Owners gauge tank steel here before surveys, sales and charters. Atlantis NDT flies a thickness measurement team in from India to the ship, and the visit is planned around cargo operations, gas-free status and the terminal's rules.

highlights.h: Tankers waiting in a sheltered roadstead
highlights.p: Ships that arrive ahead of their berth can lie in the protected bay for days, giving superintendents a window to gauge ballast tanks and deck steel before cargo operations begin or after they finish.

highlights.h: Chemical and gas carriers beside crude ships
highlights.p: Besides crude and product tankers, the area draws chemical carriers and gas ships, each with its own tank materials and entry rules that the gauging plan must respect from the first day.

highlights.h: Enhanced survey programme work in one place
highlights.p: Many ships calling here are tankers of an age where renewal and intermediate surveys require thickness reports in class formats, so gauging at Augusta supports survey planning directly.

port.h: The port of Augusta: bay, breakwaters and the Priolo industrial area
p: Augusta occupies a large natural bay on the Ionian coast of Sicily, protected from the open sea by long breakwaters and entered through channels at either end. The harbour is one of the largest sheltered anchorages in the central Mediterranean, and part of the shoreline is a naval base. Industrial quays and offshore-style jetties serve the plants of the Priolo and Melilli area, while the commercial port of Augusta handles general cargo and bulk. Together with Catania, Augusta forms the Eastern Sicilian Sea port system under a single authority.

Tankers define the port. Crude oil arrives for the refineries, refined products and chemicals leave by sea, and gas carriers and chemical ships complete the picture. For this reason Augusta is a port where ships are often large, deep-drafted and carrying cargoes that impose strict conditions on what can be done aboard. A superintendent who wants steel readings must plan around ship-to-shore transfers, cargo hose connections and the terminal's permit regime, and will usually want the work finished before a ship is released to sail.

The sheltered bay changes how inspection is planned. A ship waiting for a berth can lie at anchor in relative calm, and in settled weather a launch can reach it without much delay. Strong winds from the east or north-east can still make the outer approaches uncomfortable and slow the movement of pilots and launches. There are no tidal restrictions to speak of on the Mediterranean scale, so timing is governed by cargo, berth availability and the terminal's rules rather than by water levels. Industrial berths are often fully booked, so owners rely on agents to secure inspection time.

facilities.h: Where gauging happens around the Augusta bay
p: Augusta is an industrial and anchorage port rather than a ship repair port, and the realistic place for gauging is afloat. At industrial jetties, a tanker alongside has its ballast tanks, cargo tanks after washing and degassing, deck plating and pipework available when the terminal permits. At the anchorage, a ship waiting for its berth or between cargoes can be reached by launch, provided entry permits and gas-free certificates are in place and the weather holds.

Where a ship needs steel renewal, the docking usually happens at a yard in Malta, elsewhere in Sicily or on the mainland, and Augusta then serves as the measurement point before the passage. Gauging at the bay gives the technical team an early thickness record, which can be compared with earlier surveys to show where wastage is concentrated. The result is a steel renewal estimate that the yard can plan from facts rather than from assumptions made at the end of the voyage.
list: Industrial tanker jetties: ballast and washed cargo tanks, main deck and cargo piping, subject to terminal permits and the master's agreement
Augusta roadstead: ships waiting for a berth or between cargoes, reached by launch in settled weather
Commercial quays: general cargo and bulk ships working at the town side of the harbour
Lay-by positions inside the bay for ships idle between charters, suited to a longer programme
Nearby yards in Malta and elsewhere in Sicily used for dockings after the gauging results are known

context.h: Port state control and tank-ship regulation at Augusta
p: Port state control at Augusta is carried out by the Italian Coast Guard (Guardia Costiera) via the harbour master (Capitaneria di Porto), under the Paris MoU. Tankers carrying hazardous cargoes sit in a high-risk category for inspection, and structural condition is one of the areas where an inspector looks hardest. Corrosion in ballast tanks and on deck is a recurring topic for older tankers, and a clean set of thickness readings is one of the better defences for an owner who expects a visit.

Class surveys add their own requirements. Oil tankers, chemical carriers and bulk carriers fall under the Enhanced Survey Programme, which sets the extent of thickness measurement at each renewal and intermediate survey, and the readings must be recorded in the formats class societies expect. Gas carriers have separate requirements for their cargo containment. The EU Ship Recycling Regulation requires an Inventory of Hazardous Materials for ships calling at EU ports, and EU ETS and FuelEU Maritime shape decisions about how long older tankers stay in service.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs at Augusta
jobs.p: Most Augusta work concerns tank steel. A tanker superintendent wants to know what a ship will need at its next survey, what to tell a charterer, or what a buyer should expect. We agree the list of tanks, deck areas and pipework in advance, confirm gas-free status with the ship, and report readings by tank and structural member so the surveyor and yard can use them directly.
list: Ballast tank and deck gauging of a product tanker lying at the roadstead before its intermediate survey
Cargo tank bottom and bulkhead gauging on a chemical tanker after washing and degassing at a jetty
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a crude carrier, documented for the prospective buyer's technical team
Wall-thickness mapping of cargo and ballast piping on a tanker during a lay-by period
CAP preparation gauging for a tanker where the charterer has asked for a condition rating

logistics: Catania Fontanarossa is the nearest large airport, and a road transfer brings the team to Augusta along the coast. The crew travels from India on Schengen visas, so dates are confirmed after allowing for visa processing. The ship's agent arranges port and terminal access, and industrial berths often need names and passport details submitted in advance, so we supply those as soon as the job is confirmed.

faqs.q: Can tankers be gauged at the Augusta anchorage?
faqs.a: Yes, in settled conditions and when the ship has made the tanks safe. We reach the ship by launch, and the master confirms gas-free status and the entry permit before we go aboard. A strong swell can stop the work, so it helps to plan a spare day. Waiting time at anchor is often the longest uninterrupted window.

faqs.q: Do you gauge cargo tanks or only ballast tanks at Augusta?
faqs.a: Both, when the space is cleaned, ventilated and certified safe. Ballast tanks are accessible more often and corrode faster, so they dominate the work. Cargo tanks after washing give valuable data on bottoms and bulkheads, particularly on chemical tankers. We agree with the superintendent which tanks are realistic for the port stay.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock at Augusta?
faqs.a: Not for large ships. Augusta handles industrial, naval and cargo traffic, and dockings are normally done in Malta, elsewhere in Sicily or on the mainland. Gauging in the bay gives a thickness record that lets the owner and yard agree the steel estimate before the ship moves.

faqs.q: What documents does the ship need ready before gauging?
faqs.a: The previous thickness measurement report, the tank plan or structural drawings, the survey status, and confirmation of gas-free certificates and entry permits for the spaces to be gauged. Previous readings let us repeat the same measurement points, which shows wastage rates rather than a single snapshot.
